questions.question: How far should I take dstrader-docker now?

options.label: Validate recipe (dry-run)
options.description: Mirror-clone, run the purge on the clone, re-audit → prove real PII/IDs/keys hit 0. Non-destructive, touches nothing real. (Recommended — same gate as FF.)

options.label: Stop at the written review
options.description: Leave the findings doc + purge-paths file; you'll drive the rewrite later.

options.label: Go all the way: rewrite + force-push
options.description: Do the destructive rewrite and force-push now. (I'll still require rotation done + the prod-server re-clone coordinated first.)

questions.question: Are these repos intended to go public eventually (like the earlier FF/dstrader effort)?

options.label: Yes, prepping for public
options.description: Redact aggressively: internal IPs (192.168.x), weak DB passwords, and docker@dstrader.com all get scrubbed too.

options.label: No, staying private
options.description: Only purge real PII + the GPG keys + datadir + PDF; leave internal IPs / dev DB passwords as-is (low value on a private repo).

questions.question: How should I handle the committed GPG private keys (finding #1)?

options.label: Remove from HEAD + history
options.description: Stop committing private keys entirely; purge from all history. You re-key (new GPG keypair) and rotate the TWS/IB + mail passwords off-repo. (Recommended.)

options.label: Purge history only, keep on HEAD
options.description: Leave the current scheme that commits the keys; only remove old versions from history. (Weaker — current key still exposed to anyone with repo access.)

options.label: Leave keys, flag only
options.description: Don't touch the keys; I only purge the datadir/IDs/emails. You decide on the keys separately.

transcript_tail.text: Now I have a reliable, comprehensive picture. The remaining critical question before I can finalize severity: do the compose/properties files hold **real plaintext secret values**, and are the committed `.pgp` private keys **live** (used for prod decryption) and passphrase-protected? Let me inspect those directly.

Now the scheme is clear. The plaintext secrets in compose are weak **dev-style DB passwords** (`4321`/`654321`/`123456`/`1234` — same low-value class as FF's localhost defaults). The real concern is the **committed GPG private keys** (`dstrader_private.pgp`, `database_private.pgp`) — per `SOPS_AGE_PROD.md` these decrypt the trading engine's `.encr` files (TWS/IB login, mail password, DB backups). Let me confirm whether those keys are passphrase-protected and whether the ciphertext `.encr` files are also committed (key + ciphertext together = recoverable plaintext).

gpg isn't installed, but the structural finding is decisive: the committed **private keys sit in the repo alongside the ciphertext they decrypt** — `dstrader/prod/auto_login.properties*.encr` (TWS/IB Gateway trading login). Key + ciphertext together = the encryption is effectively defeated. That's the top-severity item regardless of passphrase. Let me confirm passphrase protection via a raw packet parse (no decryption) and verify the datadir dominates the 42 MB bloat.

The datadir is the dominant bloat: **164.7 MB across history** — including a 100 MB `ib_logfile0`, `ibdata1`, undo logs, and **`mysql-bin` binary logs** (which record every INSERT/UPDATE statement = even more raw PII than the table files). One more flag: a **17 MB `dstrader/auto_login/images/Prescription.pdf`** — an odd name for a trading repo; possibly misplaced personal/medical PII. (The passphrase parse failed on a heredoc/pipe clash — not worth re-running since gpg is absent and the remediation is identical either way.) Let me characterize that PDF and check the coordination surface (worktrees/branches), then I'll have a complete review.

I now have a complete, reliable review. Let me update task status, write the findings document into the repo (the non-destructive "review" deliverable, FF-style), then present a summary and the decisions that gate any destructive step.

Review complete. Here's what the full-history audit found across both repos (both are **private**, so nothing is live-public right now).

## `dstrader` — ✅ clean
The 2026-05-21 purge held. The 5 known IB account IDs, owner emails, AWS keys, bcrypt hashes, private IPs — all **0** across all refs, including the ~10 commits merged since. Only noise: a `FINNHUB_API_KEY=your_api_key_here` placeholder and a `claudio1@macmini.local` committer identity on 9 commits (local hostname, not real PII; optional to normalize). **No action needed.**

## `dstrader-docker` (origin `jdtogni78/dstrader-aws`) — ❌ not clean, layered exposure
Never scrubbed. Findings (full table in `docs/security/HISTORY-AUDIT.md`, paths in `docs/security/history-purge-paths.txt` — both just written, uncommitted):

| Sev | Item |
|---|---|
| **CRITICAL** | **GPG private keys committed** (`dstrader/{dstrader,database}_private.pgp`, on HEAD + history) sit in the **same repo as the ciphertext they decrypt** (`dstrader/prod/auto_login.properties*.encr` = TWS/IB Gateway trading login, mail password, DB backups). Key + ciphertext together ⇒ the trading credentials are effectively recoverable. **Treat as compromised → rotate.** |
| **HIGH** | **Raw MariaDB datadir** `datadir_dev/**` — 271 files, **164.7 MB** in history (incl. 100 MB `ib_logfile0` + `mysql-bin` binlogs). Raw `users/accounts/transactions/password_resets/personal_access_tokens` tables = FamilyFund family PII (emails, bcrypt, tokens) recoverable from binary. History-only (off HEAD). |
| MED | Real IB account IDs in text: `U5843610`(307), `DU3740548`(115), `U14940669`(56) — same IDs scrubbed from `dstrader`. |
| MED | Owner emails in text: `jdtogni1@gmail.com`(384), `jdtogni@gmail.com`(91). |
| LOW | Weak DB passwords in `docker-compose.{prod,stage}.yml` (`4321`/`654321`/`123456`); internal IPs (`192.168.0.120` ×424); `docker@dstrader.com` ×474. |
| **REVIEW** | `dstrader/auto_login/images/Prescription.pdf` (17 MB, on HEAD) — anomalous beside TWS screenshots; likely a **misplaced personal/medical document**. Not opened. |

Good news on blast radius: **0 worktrees, 3 origin branches** — far lighter than FamilyFund. The real coordination risk is the **prod server clone** (`/home/jdtogni/dev/dstrader-docker` on `192.168.0.120`) that runs live trading via cron — it must be re-cloned after any rewrite.

The recipe is drafted (purge `datadir_dev/` + the `.pgp` keys + the PDF; `--replace-text` the account IDs/emails reusing the existing off-repo redaction map). Before I build and validate it, three decisions change what I do:
